work done, services of the contractor M/s Raj Singh Rana & Co., Village Rasoolpur, Dasna, NTPC, 
Vidyut Nagar, G.B. Nagar, UP was availed of M/s Utility Powertech Ltd. (management no. 2). They 
submitted that Sh. Naresh Bhardwaj, Sh. Vijay Pal, Sh. Avnish Pratap, Sh. Jitender were employed by the 
contractor M/s Raj Singh Rana & Co. initially and Sh. Birpal and Sh. Ramesh were later hired in addition to

statutory provisions were made to the workmen by the said contractor, the details of which were supplied to 
management no. 2 by the contractor, which bear their signature. They submitted that payments were made to 
the contractor i.e. M/s Raj Singh Rana & Co. by UPL and the said contractor used to make the payments to 
the workman engaged by it. M/s Utility Powertech Ltd. (management no. 2) has no role to play except to 
ensure that the statutory payments are made to the said workmen. Hence, he submitted that claim of the 
claimant s is liable to be dismissed on this ground. 


Rejoinder has been filed by the claimants denying the averments made in the written statements of 
the management no. | & 2 and affirmed the facts mentioned in his claim statement. 


After completion of the pleadings, vide order dated 2.0.2023, following issues have been framed 


l. Whether the workman is entitled to relief claimed as per reference? (OPW). 


2. Ifthe answer of the issue no. | is affirmative, then what relief the claimant is entitled to and from 
which date? 


Now, the matter is listed for workman evidence. Workmen are required to file their affidavits of 
evidence, but, neither the workmen nor their AR has been appearing from several dates to substantiate their 
claim. 


In these circumstances, when the claimants are not interested in pursuing their case, this tribunal has 
no other option but to dismiss the claim. Hence, their claim stands dismissed. Award is passed accordingly.

l. | Workman has triggered the process for filing the claim petition after obtaining the failure report as required 
under section 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”). In his claim 
petition the workman has stated that he had been working with the respondent at the post of “Postman” 
w.e.f. 0.04.204 at the last drawn salary of Rs. 5,000/- per month. He did his job sincerely and honestly 
and had not given any complaint to the respondent. Respondent without any rhyme and reason has 
terminated his services on 26.04.20i8. Hence, he made prayer that he be reinstated in services with full back 
wages because he is not able to obtain the job.

2. Respondent herein has filed its written statement countering the submission of the claimant. He has stated 
that the claimant got the employment with the respondent through agency/contractor as outsourced delivery 
personnel for delivery of letters/dak. After expiry of the contract with the agency i.e. M/s G.A. Digital Web 
Word Pvt. Ltd. on 3i.2.20I6, the delivery work was managed by hiring the labour on daily basis as per 
the work load and requirement by the department till regular appointments were made and paid wages as per 
the minimum wages prescribed by Delhi Government from time to time. 


3. | Management had taken the preliminary objections stating that claim of the claimant is not maintainable as 
the very essence for registering the claim of the claimant under Industrial Dispute Act, l947 is lacking. The 
“Industrial Dispute” is defined by Section 200 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 as, any dispute or 
difference between employers and employers, or between employers and workmen, or between workman 
and workman, which is connected with the employment or non-employment or terms of employment or with 
the conditions of labour, of any person. The services of the claimant was no more required in view of the 
recruitment of about 740 regular Postman/Mail guard through open market competitive exam conducted as 
per relevant recruitment rules; claimant has not made the authorities of the said outsourced agency M/s G.A 
Digital Web World Pvt. Ltd. as party in the present claim for the proper and fair disposal of the case; 
instant claim is bad in law, without application of mind and in a stereotype manner hence liable to be 
dismissed; instant claim is not maintainable in view of the judgments passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court 
in the case of State of Karnataka vs. Uma Devi & Ors. [2006 (4) SCC I], as the applicant has no cause of 
action for filing the present claim. Infact, management has denied the master and servant relationship. He 
submitted that after expiry of the contract with the agencies, claimant himself offered to be engaged on daily 
wage basis as and when required. Hence, the question of his dis-engagement does not arise. On merit, he has 
denied the averments of the claimant’s claim and submitted that claim is liable to be dismissed. 


4.  Rejoinder has been filed the rejoinder denying the averments made in the written statement and affirmed the 
fact mentioned in his claim statement. 


5. After completion of the pleadings, vide order dated 26.07.209, following issues have been framed i.e.- 


(i) | Whether the proceeding is maintainable. 


(ii) Whether there exists any employer and employee relationship between management and the 
workman. 


(iii) Whether the service of the workman was illegally terminated in violation of provisions of 
Section 25-F of the ID Act. 


(iv) To what relief the workman is entitled to. 


6. In order to prove and disprove the issues, both the claimant and the management have examined one 
witness each. Claimant himself has entered into the witness box and reiterated the facts in his examination 
in chief as stated by him in his claim statement. He has relied upon three documents i.e.- 


(i) Ex. WWI/l & Ex. WWI/2: Copy of demand letter dated 23.05.208 alongwith postal receipts. 
(ii) Ex. WWI/3: Claim filed on 3.06.208 before the Labour Commissioner (Central). 


7. Workman in his cross-examination has admitted that he came to know of the vacancy from 0.0!.20l4 
through one Girish Chand Joshi. He joined the management on 0.04.20l4. He also admitted that no 
advertisement, application form, appointment letter or identity card was issued to him. He stated that no 
salary slip, PF, ESI, DA, HRA or other services benefits were ever provided to him. He submitted that he 
never appeared in any such written test. He was getting his remuneration after each I5 days through 
vouchers. He denied having any knowledge of M/s G.A. Digital Web World Pvt. Ltd. His services were 
terminated on 04.04.208. 

8. In rebuttal, management has filed the affidavit of evidence of Sh. Sajid Vishal, Assistant Superintendent 
exhibited as Ex. MWI/A. He has deposed the facts, stating that Department of Posts had issued tender for 
providing skilled, semi-skilled and un-skilled man power in PO & RMS Offices of Delhi Circle on 
different dates and was awarded the contract to M/s G.A. Digital Web Word Pvt. Ltd. He further stated 
that workman was provided by M/s G.A. Digital Web Word Pvt. Ltd. agencies/contractor as outsourced 
delivery personnel for delivery of letter at Jhilmil Head Post Office, Delhi-!l0095. On account of filling up 
of the said posts by making regular appointment, service of the workman was not required. Even after, 
expiry of the contract with the agency M/s G.A. Digital Web Word Pvt. Ltd. on 3.2.206, the delivery 
work was managed by hiring the labour on daily rate basis as per the work load and requirement by the 
department till regular appointments were made and was paid wages as per the minimum wages prescribed 
by Delhi Government time to time. He also stated that during the visit by then Postmaster, Jhilmil HO, a

total of 346 undelivered mail was recovered from the Jhilmil Industrial Area on 4.02.205, which shows 
extreme delinquency in duty by the claimant. He further said that there was an opportunity to the workman 
to appear in the competitive exam conducted by Delhi Postal Circle, but, said opportunity has not been 
availed by the workman. The extended terms and conditions of the tender were expired on dated 
3.2.20I6. He has relied upon two documents i.e.: 


(i) Ex. १७५७७४]/] :] लाल of authorization dated 20..2023. 


(ii) Ex. WWI/2: tender document semi skilled manpower in Delhi Postal Circle by 
M/s G.A. Digital Web Word Pvt. Ltd. (Colly.) 


9. Management’s witness in his cross-examination has admitted that workman was not given any appointment 
letter. He admitted that domestic enquiry was conducted against the claimant by the vigilance team of 
management. 


0. So far so, issues no. | & 2 are concerned. The admission of the management that even after the expiry of 
the contract, he continued take the service of the claimant itself establishes the relationship of employer- 
employee between them. Though, it is an admitted fact that initially the claimant’s services were hired 
through contractor i.e. M/s G.A Digital Web World Pvt. Ltd., but, later on after expiry of the contract, his 
services have been continuously availed by the management and the claimant was paid the minimum 
pay scale. 


ll. Moreover, the management has taken plea that enquiry was conducted by the vigilance team of the 
management, but, the management has stated that in the written statement that there exist no relationship 
of employer and employee, so, how the vigilance team has conducted the enquiry and even continued his 
service till April, 208, though, the 346 undelivered mail has been found on 4.02.20]5. 


2. In the light of aforesaid evidence and admission of the management regarding conducting of the vigilance 
inquiry, claimant has proved relationship of employer and employee between the management and the 
workman. Therefore, the objection in this regard regarding the non-existence does not stand anywhere. 
Therefore, both issues regarding the maintainability of the petition as well as the existence of employer- 
employee relationship goes against the management and in favour of the workman. 


3. Now, come to the issue no. 3 i.e. “Whether the service of the workman was illegally terminated by the 
management in violation of provision of Section 25-F of the I.D. Act”. Claimant’s claim is that his services 
have been terminated illegally on 26.04.208 after withholding the salary of month of April, 208. 


4. Before dealing with this issue, the texts of Sections 2(00), 25F, G and H of the Act are required to be 
reproduced herein: 


Section 2(00): 


“retrenchment” means the termination by the employer of the service of a 
workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by 
way of disciplinary action, but does not include- 


(a) voluntary retirement of the workman; or 

(b) retirement of the workman on reaching the age of superannuation if the 
contract of employment between the employer and the workman concerned 
contains a stipulation in that behalf; or 

(c) termination of the service of the workman as a result of the on-renewal of the 
contract of employment between the employer and the workman concerned 
on its expiry or of such contract being terminated under a stipulation in that 
behalf contained therein; or] 

(d) termination of the service of a workman on the ground of continued ill- 
health; ] 


25F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen: No workman employed in any 
industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer 
shall be retrenched by that employer until-

(a) the workman has been given one month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for 
retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu 
of such notice, wages for the period of the notice; 

(b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be 
equivalent to fifteen days' average pay [for every completed year of continuous service] 
or any part thereof in excess of six months; and 

(c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government [or such 
authority as may be specified by the appropriate Government by notification in the 
Official Gazette]. 

25G. Procedure for retrenchment.—Where any workman in an industrial establishment, 
who is a citizen of India, is to be retrenched and he belongs to a particular category of 
workmen in that establishment, in the absence of any agreement between the employer 
and the workman in this behalf, the employer shall ordinarily retrench the workman who 
was the last person to be employed in that category, unless for reasons to be recorded the 
employer retrenches any other workman. 


25H. Re-employment of retrenched workmen.—Where any workmen are retrenched, 
and the employer proposes to take into his employ any persons, he shall, in such manner 
as may be prescribed, give an opportunity 4[to the retrenched workmen who are citizens 
of India to offer themselves for re-employment and such retrenched workman] who offer 
themselves for re-employment shall have preference over other persons. 


5. | From the perusal of the above sections, it is apparent that the claimant/workman as defined under section 
2(s) has not been given the absolute protection against his retrenchment/termination. Section 2(00) of the 
Act defines the word “retrenchment”. Clause-(a), (b), (bb) and (c) have been carved out the exception 
from the definition of the retrenchment. Clause 2 (bb) which has been inserted by the Act 49 of 984 
w.e.f. 8.08.!984 had stated that when the services of the workman as a result of the non-renewal of the 
contract of employment between the employer and the workman concerned on its expiry. 


6. If the person has not come in any of the category then the claimant who has completed one year of 
continuous service cannot be retrench without compliance of the condition enumerated in section 25-F of 
the Act. Section 25-F of the Act infers that the claimants have no absolute right to remain in the 
employment of the management. The management can discontinue or retrench the workmen who have 
completed not less than one year of service under the employer if he has given a one month notice in 
writing indicating the reason for retrenchment and the period of notice has expired or he has paid the 
wages in lieu of notice period. The second condition is that the retrenchment compensation shall also be 
paid equivalent to 5-days of average pay for every completed year of continuous service. Besides this, 
appropriate government shall also be informed regarding the retrenchment. 


7. Here, in the present case, it is already established that after expiry of the contract with M/s G.A Digital 
Web World Pvt. Ltd., the service of the workman was continuously taken by the respondent and he had 
been paid the monthly remuneration as per minimum wages. So, agreement of M/s G.A Digital Web 
World Pvt. Ltd. has come to an end on 3].2.206, thereafter, the services has been continued till 
25.04.208. Management’s witness has not given any answer why the workman had worked till 
25.04.208 and has not come up for further cross-examination after l0.l2.2024, meaning thereby, the 
assertion of the claimant is true that he had lastly worked on 25.04.208 with the management. 


8. It is settled legal position that the claimant has to prove that he has been continuously working with the 
respondent for 240 days in a calendar year. Since, management has not brought any evidence contrary to 
the fact that the workman has not worked for 240 days continuously in a calendar year than this Tribunal 
has no option except to believe the version of the claimant that he has worked continuously l6.2.206 to 
25.04.208 directly with the management. 


9. Since, it is an admitted case that the management has not made compliance of the provision of Section 25- 
F of the Act, the termination of the workman is held to be illegal. Hence, issue no. 3 goes against the 
management and in favour of the workman.

RELIEF 


20. Now, the question arises as to what relief is given to the workman. In the present case, workman claimed 
that he had served with the management from 0.04.204 to 25.04.208.Normally, when the termination of 
the claimant is held to be illegal, reinstatement with full back wages shall be given to the workman. It has 
been held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in the case titled as Employers, Management of central 
P& D Inst. Ltd. vs. Union of India & Another, AIR 2005 Supreme Court 633 that it is not always 
mandatory to order reinstatement even after the termination is held illegal. Instead, compensation can be 
granted by the industrial adjudicator. 


2l. However, in the peculiar circumstances where the management’s stand is that 746 posts were 
recruited through competitive examination and the claimant’s services were availed only for stock gap 
arrangement for delivery of the post, relief of reinstatement with full back wages is not appropriate. Given 
the circumstances where the workman did the work for four years with the respondent management either 
through contractor or directly, a lump sum compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lac only) is 
considered to be an appropriate relief. Hence, management is hereby directed to pay compensation of Rs. 
5,00,000/- to the claimant within two months of notification of this award, failing which the management 
shall also pay interest @ 9% per annum on the aforesaid amount from the date of award until realization. A 
copy of this award be sent to the appropriate government for notification under section |7 of the Act. The 
file is consigned to record room.

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 
0 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India, through the Ministry of 
Labour and Employment, vide its Order No. L-420/l69/20I2-IR(DU) dated 28.02.20i3, has been 
pleased to refer the following dispute between and for adjudication by this Tribunal in the following terms: 


“Whether the action of the management of NDMC in not granting compassionate employment to 
Shri Ashok Kumar S/o Late Shri Bhurey Lal is legal and justified? If not, what relief the 
workman is entitled to?” 


At the outset, it is important to mention here that the present case reflects the misuse of the 
legalmachineryfor appointment on compassionate grounds. 


In pursuance of the reference, the claimant appeared and filed his claim statement. He stated that his 
father Sh. BhureyLal, who was working with the management, expired on 9.02.2004. Thereafter, the 
claimant applied for appointment on compassionate grounds. He alleged that although the management had 
given compassionate appointment to 92 applicants, his claim was rejected without assigning any reasons. 


The management granted employment in its Fire Department to 9 persons in 2004, 8 in 2005, in 
2006, 5 in 2007, 44 in 2008, 80 in 2009, and 63 in 200. It also granted employment in its Civil 
Department to 72 persons in 2004, 8 in 2005, 48 in 2006, 38 in 2007, 43 in 2008, 33 in 2009, 
and7 in 200.According to him, despite large-scale appointments during the said period, he was denied 
compassionate appointment. Being aggrieved, he approached the conciliation officer and upon failure of 
conciliation, the present reference was made to this Tribunal. Therefore, the claimant has filed his claim 
seeking employment on compassionate grounds in lieu of services rendered by his deceased father. 


In response, the management filed a written statement stating that the present claim is a sheer 
misuse and abuse of the processof law as no right accrues in favour of the claimant as a matter of 
fundamental right to claim employment under the category of compassionate grounds. In fact, there are 
certain guidelines drafted by the department as per the DoPT Guidelines and other provisions under which 
such employments are governed,and the claimant did not fulfill the prescribed eligibility criteria. It was 
further stated that the present reference has been made in a mechanical and stereotype manner without 
considering the stand of the management. Hence, the management prayed for dismissal of the present 
claim. 


A rejoinder had also been filed by the claimant where he denied the averments made by the 
management in its written statement and affirmed the averments in his claim statement. 


From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 26..203: 


l. Whether the action of the management of NDMC in not granting compassionate employment 
to Shri Ashok Kumar S/o Late Shri Bhurey Lal is legal and justified? 


2. Ifnot, what relief the workman is entitled to?” 


To prove his case, the claimant examined himself as WWI. He reiterated the facts stated in the 
claim statement and relied upon the following documents: 


l. Minutes of meeting of the committee constituted for examining the cases of appointments on 
compassionate grounds. (Ex. ४४/७४७।/।) 


2. List of recommended cases of compassionate appointments duly attested by the management. 
(Ex. ४४७४ ।/2) 


3. List of rejected cases of compassionate appointments duly attested by the management (Ex. 
Wwi/3). 


9388 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : AUGUST 5, 2026/ SHRAVAN 24, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


4. List of deferred cases of compassionate appointments duly attested by the management. (Ex. 
१४४७ ॥/4). 


5. List of daily wagers appointed during 2004. (Ex. WW ॥/5). 
6. Death certificate of the deceased father of the claimant (Mark A). 


7. Family details and correspondences with the management regarding compassionate appointment. 
(Mark B). 


During cross-examination, the claimant admitted that he raised the dispute regarding compassionate 
appointment after 8 years of his father’s death. He further admitted that he had no knowledge of the 
grounds and criteriaconsidered for compassionate appointment. He further deposed that his father passed 
away leavingbehind four dependents, namely himself, his elder brother, his elder sister and his younger 
brother. He admitted that his siblings were aware of his claim, however no ‘No Objection Certificate’ had 
been filed by them. 


In rebuttal, the management also examined one witness, Ms. Meena Kaushal, Deputy Director 
(Civil and Electrical Establishment). She deposed that the management, while considering and 
recommending numerous applications of such candidates, follows the guidelines of the DoPT, such as the 
seniority of the deceased, his age at the time of death, the dependents left behind by him, particularly 
unmarried daughters, the number of years of service left at the time of death, physical disability of the 
applicant, etc. She stated that the lists of recommended, rejected, and deferred cases were already on record 
and had been exhibited by the claimant himself. 


During her cross-examination, the witness admitted that the father of the claimant, Sh. Bhurey lal, was 
working as a Mate in the Civil Engineering department and expired on 9.02.2004. she further admitted 
that the claimant’s application for his appointment on compassionate grounds was rejected as per the policy 
and guidelines of DoPT after due consideration. She also admitted that the claimant’s younger brother, Sh. 
Sitaram, was receiving pension till attaining the age of 25 years. 


During the course of proceedings, some startling facts has been emerged. On 0.03.2025, the management 
produced the personal file of the claimant. It was revealed that the claimant’s younger brother, Sh. Sitaram, 
was shown to have received pension till 204 and was shown to be |5 years old at the time of their father’s 
death. However, the personal file containedmultiple affidavits with different date of birth of Sh. Sitaram 
and other family members. In one affidavit, Sh.Sitaramwas shown to be 22 years old at the time of death of 
his father.In the application addressed to the secretary, NDMC, seeking appointment on compassionate 
grounds, the claimant declared his own date of birth as 05.0.985.The elder brother’s date of birth was 
shown as .09.975, while the younger brother was shown to be born in 995. The date of birth of her 
elder sister, Smt. Krishna was shown as |5.05.97. The affidavit of Sh. Rajinder Kumar dated 07.06.2004 
states that his younger brother, Sh. Sitaram, was born on 0.2.!995. Another affidavit of the claimant, Sh. 
Ashok Kumar, also dated 07.06.2004, shows the date of birth of Smt. Krishna, the claimant’s sister, as 
0.0.985. In yet another affidavit of Sh. Rajinder Kumar dated 22..2004, he declared his own date of 
birth as 04.07.978. In another affidavit, Sh. Sitaramwas shown to have been born on 20.0.982, while the 
applicant, Sh. Ashok Kumar, was shown to have been born on 05.07.979. 


Further, the noting on the personal file showed that both Sh. Rajinder Kumar and the claimant Sh. Ashok 
Kumar were married, whereas Sh. Sitaram was shown as unmarried. The pension record broughts by the 
management reveal that Sh. Sitaram was shown to be entitled for family pension till he attained the age of 
25 years. His date of birth was taken on the basis of a medical examination as 989. Neither the year 982 
nor !995was takeninto consideration. Except for a medical certificate furnished by management, nothing is 
foundrecord to establish his age. There is no document to show whether any x-ray or a bone density test 
was conductedfor determining his age, and no such report or film in this regard has been placed on record. 
No reason has been assigned as to why the department deemed it necessary to medically examine Sh. 
Sitaram to establish his correct age. 


The mention of different age of Sh. Sitaram at different places, along with different age of the claimant Sh. 
Ashok Kumar in their affidavits, makes the claimant’s case doubtful. The claimant didn’t disclose at any 
point that he was married or unmarried. At some places, he is shown to have been born in !979, while at 
other places, his year of birth is mentioned as 985, and the noting on record suggests that he was married. 


Therefore, it appears that the claimant attempted to secure dual benefits, pension benefits to the younger 
brother up to the age of 25, despite claiming his year of birth as 995 or earlier, i.e., |982, and appointment 
on compassionate grounds, even though the claimant was already married, asnone of the several affidavits 
disclose the marital status of the claimant.

to compassionate appointment. Hence, issue no. | is decided against the claimant and in favour of the 
management. Consequent thereto, issue no. 2 also goes in favor of the management. 


In light of the above findings, the reference is answered against the claimant and in favor of the 
management. Accordingly, the claim of the claimant stands dismissed. A copy of this award be sent to the 
appropriate government for notification under section 47 of the I.D Act. The case file is consigned to

has completed 240 working days with the management no. 2 in a single year. Ld. Counsel for the 
claimant submitted that he would produce a chart to clarify the working days of the claimant; 
however, instead of producing the chart, he has called the workman. He emphasized that it was a 
fixed term contract for two years and the respondent has terminated the workman illegally. 


Record of the present case states that claim was filed by the claimant, stating that he was 
appointed by the management no. 2 on the post of “Lineman” on |!.08.2020, and his last drawn 
wages were Rs. 9,864/- per month. It is the management no. 2 who has deputed to workman in the 
management no. |. He used to work sincerely; however, management no. 2 had illegally and 
unjustifiably terminated his services on 3.03.202! without any rhyme or reason and without paying 
the earned wages for the month of Jan., Feb., and March, 202! and without giving any notice or notice 
pay to him. Hence, he filed the claim. 


Both the managements have filed their respective written statements. Issues were framed on 
29.08.2022. On the last date of hearing, this Tribunal had noted down that workman has failed to 
complete the 240 days in a preceding year to his termination. 


For ready reference, the provision of Sections 2A, 2(00) & 25F of the Industrial Disputes 
Act, 947 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) are required to be reproduced herein:- 


Section 2A: 
[2A. Dismissal, etc. of an individual workman to be deemed to be an industrial dispute 


[()] Where any employer discharges, dismisses, retrenches or otherwise 
terminates the services of an individual workman, any dispute or difference 
between that workman and his employer connected with, or arising out of, such 
discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination shall be deemed to be an 
industrial dispute notwithstanding that no other workman nor any union of 
workmen is a party to the dispute.] 


[(2)] Notwithstanding anything contained in section /0, any such workman as 
is specified in sub-section (7) may, make an application direct to the Labour 
Court or Tribunal for adjudication of the dispute referred to therein after the 
expiry of forty-five days from the date he has made the application to the

Conciliation Officer of the appropriate Government for conciliation of the 
dispute, and in receipt of such application the Labour Court or Tribunal shall 
have powers and jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the dispute, as if it were a 
dispute referred to it by the appropriate Government in accordance with the 
provisions of this Act and all the provisions of this Act shall apply in relation to 
such adjudication as they apply in relation to an industrial dispute referred to it 
by the appropriate Government. 


(3) The application referred to in sub-section (2) shall be made to the Labour 
Court or Tribunal before the expiry of three years from the date of discharge, 
dismissal, retrenchment or otherwise termination of service as specified in sub- 
section (/)). 


Section 2(00): 


“retrenchment” means the termination by the employer of the service of a 
workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by 
way of disciplinary action, but does not include- 


(a) voluntary retirement of the workman; or 

(b) retirement of the workman on reaching the age of superannuation if the 
contract of employment between the employer and the workman concerned 
contains a stipulation in that behalf; or 

(bb) termination of the service of the workman as a result of the on-renewal of the 

contract of employment between the employer and the workman concerned on 
its expiry or of such contract being terminated under a stipulation in that 
behalf contained therein; or] 


(c) termination of the service of a workman on the ground of continued ill-health; ] 
Section 25F: 


25F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen.- No workman employed 
in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under 
an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until- 
(a) the workman has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the 
reasons for retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has 
been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period of the notice; 
(b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which 
shall be equivalent to fifteen days' average pay [for every completed year of 
continuous service] or any part thereof in excess of six months; and 
(c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate government [or 
such authority as may be specified by the appropriate Government by notification in 
the Official Gazette. ] 


Provision of Section 2A of the Act has been carved out in the year 967 when the 
amendment has been made whereby dismissal, retrenchment or termination of an individual 
workman is deemed to be the industrial dispute. Subsequently, another amendment was 
made in 200, whereby the appropriate government was relieved from applying of its minds 
while making a reference to the Tribunal in cases of discharge, dismissal and retrenchment 
of the individual workman. The workman may directly file the application after taking the 
recourse of conciliation upon failure of the conciliation proceedings after 45 days. The next 
rider is that the application must be filed before the Tribunal within three years from the 
date of discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination. 


Section 2(00) of the Act defines the retrenchment by the employer of the service of 
a workman for any reason whatsoever. However, five exceptions have been carved out 
where such termination does not fall within the definition of retrenchment. 


Section 25F of the Act imposes certain conditions upon the employer before 
terminating the employee. The first condition is that the workman shall be given the one 
month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and the period of notice. 
The second condition is that the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment,

compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days' average pay [for every completed 
year of continuous service] or any part thereof in excess of six months. The third condition 
is that the notice in the prescribed manner is served upon the appropriate government. The 
section 25F begins with the word that “No workman employed in any industry who has 
been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer”. Meaning thereby- 
the person can be retrenched without complying the condition (a), (b) & (c), if he has not 
completed one year of continuous service. 


Section 25-B of the Act defines the term “continuous service”. Clause-2 of the said 
section states that where a workman is not in continuous service within the meaning of 
clause () for a period of one year or six months, he shall be deemed to be in continuous 
service under an employer. Clause-2 of section 25-B of the Act is also required to be 
reproduced herein- 

Clause-2 of Section 25-B of the Act- 


(2) where a workman is not in continuous service within the meaning of clause 
(I) for a period of one year or six months, he shall be deemed to be in continuous 
service under an employer- 


(a) for a period of one year, if the workman, during a period of twelve 
calendar months preceding the date with reference to which calculation is to be 
made, has actually worked under the employer for not less than- 


(i) one hundred and ninety days in the case of a workman employed below 
ground in a mine; 


(ii) two hundred and forty days, in any other case; 


(b) for a period of six months, if the workman, during a period of six calendar 
months preceding the date with reference to which calculation is to be made, has 
actually worked under the employer for not less than- 


(i) ninety-five days, in the case of a workman employed below ground in 
a mine; 


(ii) one hundred and twenty days, in any other case. 


Explanation.- For the purpose of clause (2), the number of days on which a 
workman has actually worked under an employer shall include the days on 
which- 


(i) _ he has been laid-off under an agreement or as permitted by standing 
orders made under the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 
946 (20 of 946), or under the Act or under any other law applicable to 
the industrial establishment; 


(ii) he has been on leave with full wages, earned in the previous year; 


(iii) he has been absent due to temporary disablement caused by 
accident arising out of and in the course of his employment; and 


(iv) in the case of a female, she has been on maternity leave; so, however, 
that the total period of such maternity leave does not exceed twelve 
weeks. ] 


Here, the claimant himself has stated in his claim statement that he worked on the 
post of “Lineman” with the management no. 2 from |.08.2020 to 3.03.202]. If the period 
of work is counted from !.08.2020, then, the total number of days worked by the claimant 
with the management no. 2 is less than 240 days. The claimant actually worked only 233

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub —section (2A) of 
Section 0 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947) Government Of India through the 
Ministry of Labour, vide its Order No.L-!202//2005-IR(B-ID) dated 30/05/2005 has been pleased 
to refer the following dispute between the employer i.e. management of Bank of India, Zonal Office, 
Dhanbad and their workman namely Sri Subhas Saw for adjudication by this Tribunal: 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of Bank of India, Dhanbad Zone, Dhanbad in 
terminating Sh. Subhas Saw from the services of the Bank in subordinate cadre i.e. as 
Driver from May, 2004 is justified? If not, to what relief the concerned workman is 
entitled ?” 


2; On perusal of the case record it transpires that previously the present reference was decided 
in favour of the workman vide order dated 30.03.20I5 but when the same was challenged by the 
management before the Hon’ble High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi in W.P. (L) No. 4397 of 205, 
the Hon’ble Court was pleased to set aside the Award passed by this Tribunal vide order dated 
02.07.20i9 and the matter was remanded to this Tribunal for taking fresh decision after hearing both 
sides. 


3. The case of the workman as per the written statement filed on his behalf is that the workman 
Subhas Saw has been working as permanent Driver of Bank of India since 0..99] continuously 
to the satisfaction of the management. He has been working as Driver and driving vehicles of the 
Bank for the purpose of business of the bank and management is the owner of aforesaid vehicles. He 
has been rendering service and producing goods for the benefit of the Bank Management but the 
management had been paying him wages at the rate of Rs. 340/- and subsequently Rs. |700/- from 
0.0.994. The concerned workman represented before the management several times for his 
proper wages and benefit at par with other employees of the Bank and at the initial stage the 
petitioner was assured by the management for regularization and wages at par with other employees 
and he waited on the assurance of the management but unfortunately all of sudden the management 
terminated the service of the workman on May 2004 by stopping him from duty. The petitioner had 
put in continuous service from 0.li.99l to May 2004 and had put in more than 240 days 
attendance in each calendar year. His service was terminated when he insisted for regularization and 
proper wages. He was terminated without following the mandatory provision of Section 25-F of the 
I.D. Act. He represented before the management for illegal and arbitrary termination and seeing no 
other alternative raised industrial dispute that ended in failure and that ultimately resulted in the 
present reference. The action of the management in terminating the services of the concerned 
workman was illegal, arbitrary and against the principle of natural justice as well as against the 
provision of Section 25-F of the I.D. Act and he prayed to answer the reference in favour of the 
workman. 


4. On the other hand the case of the management as per the written statement cum rejoinder is 
that the present reference is not legally maintainable. The issued reference for adjudication is vague, 
indefinite and cannot be adjudicated. Sri Subhas Saw has filed his written statement describing 
himself as disputant claiming that he was the workman of the Bank. No employer-employee 
relationship exists between the disputant and the Bank Management. He was never selected by the 
Bank Selection Committee of the Bank as per the Recruitment Rules of the management. He was 
never employed as employee of the Bank. As per the Regulation 26 of the Bank of India Service 
Regulations, !979 the Bank Officers in Scale IV to VII are allowed to use the Bank Car for personal 


[भाग ]--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 5, 2026/ श्रावण 24, 948 940I 


purpose for which they require personal driver also and to enable them to engage for personal driver 
the wages to be paid to the personal drivers are also reimbursed by the Bank at specified level. Such 
drivers are identified and engaged purely on personal basis without any supervision and control of 
the Bank and similarly there is no service condition fixed by the Bank for personal driver and 
therefore there is no employer-employee relationship between the Bank and the said driver at any 
point of time. The petitioner was engaged by the Bank Officers in their personal capacity from time 
to time to drive the car provided to them by the Bank for their personal purpose. Such agreement was 
entirely between the Officer concerned and the petitioner in their personal capacities. The petitioner 
has worked as personal driver of the Bank Officers for certain period and he is advancing his claims 
to treat him as an employee of the Bank and is demanding for his absorption in the employment of 
the company. The petitioner was personal driver in personal capacity, he cannot vest any right or 
claim on the latter for bank employment. He was neither appointed nor terminated by the Bank from 
the services of the Bank and therefore the question of adjudication for termination of the services of 
the petitioner does not arise and he is not entitled to any relief. In rejoinder it has been stated that the 
petitioner has never worked as permanent driver of the Bank of India and he was never appointed as 
a driver of the Bank and again it has repeated the facts already stated and denied the stand taken by 
the workman in his W/S. 


5. The petitioner has also filed a separate rejoinder to the W/S of the management in which he 
has denied all the claim of the management. 


6. Issue 


“Whether the action of the management of Bank of India, Dhanbad Zone, Dhanbad in 
terminating Sh.Subhas Saw from the services of the Bank in subordinate cadre i.e. as Driver from 
May, 2004 is justified? If not, to what relief the concerned workman is entitled?” 


7. In support of his case the workman has adduced the documents related to his salary from 
August [992 to June 999 and Log Book from June 2003 to April 2006. 


8. No oral evidence has been adduced from the side of the workman. 

9. On the other hand the management has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence. 

0. Heard both sides and perused the materials on record. 

Il. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the workman has submitted that he had been working as 


Driver in Bank of India since 0i.l!.99l and had been driving vehicles as employee of the 
management but he was not being paid monthly wages at par with the permanent employees and 
therefore he raised the issue and being annoyed by the same the management illegally terminated his 
services w.e.f. May 2004 without issuing any reason and therefore prayed to set aside the termination 
and reinstate him. 


I2; On the other hand the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the management has submitted that the 
petitioner was never appointed by the management as employee of the Bank nor he was ever issued 
any appointment letter and therefore no employer-employee relationship exists between them. As per 
the regulation 26 of the Bank of India the Bank Officers in Scale IV to VII were allowed to use 
Bank’s Car for personal purpose and they were also allowed to engage personal driver as per their 
requirement and the wages to be paid to them by the said officer were to be reimbursed by the bank 
up to the specified level and so the personal driver of the bank’s executive is not the employee of the 
bank and the present petitioner accordingly is not entitled to any relief in this case and has no right to 
regularization or reinstatement. 


3. On perusal of the documents adduced from the side of the workman though not exhibited it 
transpires that there are two types of documents, first one is the copy of register of the Log Book 
from June 2003 to April 2006 of the Bank of India and the second one is the details of salary given 
to the petitioner Subhas Saw from August !992 to June 999 which also bears the signature of the 
petitioner Subhas Saw after receiving the payment in each and every month and the second set of 
documents are the copy of Motor Car Log Book from June 2003 to April 2006 and it also contains 
the name of Subhas Saw with the number of vehicle. This also contains the details of Journey, 
Kilometers etc. 


These documents have not been disputed by the management and in its W/S the 
management has admitted the employment of Subhas Saw as personal driver of the Bank Executive. 


4. In view of the documents as well as the period of engagement of the petitioner Subhas Saw 
from year 99! to May 2004 it is established that he has continued his job for quite long period and 
therefore the relationship of the employer-employee is created between the petitioner and the 


9402 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : AUGUST 5, 2026/ SHRAVAN 24, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


management even though he was not issued any appointment letter and the above documents add the 
authenticity as well as genuineness of the case of the workman and in such circumstances the action 
of the management of Bank of India , Dhanbad Zone, Dhanbad in terminating Sri Subhas Saw from 
the services of the Bank in subordinate cadre i.e. as Driver from May, 2004 is held not at all justified 
and he is entitled to reinstatement by way of relief but as this is year of 2026 and about 2 decades 
have passed, the direction of reinstatement is not appropriate rather the management is directed to 
make payment of Rs. 0 Lakh as compensation to the workman Subhas Saw within a period of 3 
months from the date of publication of this Award. The reference is answered accordingly. 


Let the copies of Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour & Employment, 
Government of India, New Delhi for information and notification.

SCHEDULE 


“Whether the supply worker Shri Rajesh Kumar has been unjustifiably denied the 
seniority in the empanelment list drawn from Contract workers of DVC, BTPS despite 
working from 987 in the BTPS, DVC plant? If yes, then what remedies he is entitled 
to?” 


2 The case of the workman as per the written statement filed on his behalf is that the worker 
concemed was engaged as a Supply worker under a contractor namely M/s S.P. Yadav at the Bokaro 
Thermal Power Station of Damodar Valley Corporation, Bokaro since February, !987. On 
30.08.992 and thereafter on 7.09.993 a memorandum of settlement/tripartite agreement was 
reached in between the parties duly participated by the management of DVC, The Contractor, DVC 
Labour Union, Bokaro Thermal and United Contactors’ Workers Union, Bokaro memorandum of 
settlement/tripartite agreement, the Chief Engineer-l, BTPS on 0.09.998 prepared a 
panel/seniority list of the contract labourers at BTPS but the name of the concerned worker was not 
included in the said list. On the date of preparation of panel i.e. on 0.07.998 the cut off date was 
28.02.997 and the total number of man days till cut off date of the worker comes to total of 298] 
days, therefore as per the number of days worked by the worker concerned the position of the worker 
in the panel list should have been determined at Sl. No. 5. The contractual labourers with less 
number of man days than that of the worker concerned have been empanelled and subsequently 
regularized in the service and therefore the worker concerned has right to claim in the seniority list 
of the panel of workers. The letter dated 9.07.2007 issued by the management is arbitrary, malafide, 
illegal and contrary to determination as made by them and therefore the worker has suffered the 
monetary benefits as per settlement dated 30.08.992 and 7.09.993 and accordingly the workman 
is entitled for grant of benefits with retrospective effect. The workman also approached the Regional 
Labour Commissioner (Central) for deciding the issue and on |2.04.2002 after making enquiry with 
regard to the claim of the petitioner and going through the detail report of the Assistant Labour 
Commissioner with regard to the total number of mandays/attendance of the petitioner from 987 to 
200l at the Operation & Maintenance Department of BTPS made a request to the management 
concemed to implement the settlement during 30 days and submit the implementation report and at 
last it was prayed to direct the concerned management to place the name of the concerned workman 
in the appropriate place i.e. at Serial No. 5 in Seniority list of [998 as per the seniority retirement by 
Regional Labour Commissioner on the basis of man days and absorb the worker concerned as 
regular employee as identical worker with much lesser number of man days and grant all the 
monetary benefits as per the memorandum of settlement dated 30.08.992 and 7.09.993.

during the same job which his co-worker Sri Y.P. Singh and Kapildeo Singh are doing with I“& 2"

3. On the other hand the case of the management as per the written statement cum rejoinder 
dated 0.2.2002 filed on its behalf is that Sri Sushil Kumar Singh initially was appointed under the 
Coal Control Organization and subsequently on its closure Sri Singh was transferred and posted at 
Dhansar Colliery in the month of November 999. Sri Singh is presently designated as Sampling 
Attendant in Grade “F” under SLU Grade “E”. While he was posted at Dhansar Colliery his existing 


940 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : AUGUST 5, 2026/ SHRAVAN 24, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


designation and scale of pay was that of sampling attendant and hence he has been posted to Dhansar 
Colliery siding to look after the job of loading of wagons. His job included only to look after loading 
of wagons which is not the same job as that of loading clerk. It was further submitted that since Sri 
Singh is a sampling attendant, he was allowed to look after the job of loading of wagon and as such 
in no way Sri Singh be considered for regularization on the post of loading clerk as the scale of pay 
as well as the grade of loading clerk differs from the sampling attendant in which the workman is 
still working without any force by the management. It was further submitted that the workman has 
claimed his regularization as Loading Supervisor/ Loading Munshi which is not in tune with the 
actual state of affairs. The workman should either have claimed for regularization as loading 
supervisor or for regularization as loading Munshi in particular but inspite of that workman has 
claimed for regularization on the basis of either of which is illegal and ill motivated. He cannot claim 
regularization as loading supervisor/loading Munshi as his nature of job differs from that of 
sampling attendant. By way of rejoinder the management has admitted the case of the workman to 
the extent that he was transferred to Dhansar Colliery in November |999 and under the office order 
as mentioned but he has further stated that it is incorrect to say as would be evident in the office 
order dated 28.!.999 that he was asked to work as loading supervisor. The management has denied 
the rest of the stand taken by the workman in different paragraphs of the written statement and lastly 
prayed that Award be passed that the workman concerned is not entitled to any regularization as 
claimed. 


4. A separate rejoinder has also been filed on behalf of the workman denying all the claims and 
stands taken by the management in its written statement and repeating the claim of the regularization 
of the workman. 


a Issue 


“Whether the action of the management of M/s BCCL in not regularizing Sri Sushil Kumar 
Singh as Loading Supervisor/Loading Munshi is fair and justified? If not, to what relief is the 
concerned workman entitled and from what date?” 


6. In support of his case the workman has submitted the following documentary evidence: 
Exhibit १४-। — Copy of Office Order dated 07.07.2006 
Exhibit W-2 — Copy of Office Order dated 3.07.2006 
Exhibit W-3 — Copy of Office Order dated 8.07.2006 
Exhibit W-4 — Copy of Office Order dated 7.08.2006 
Exhibit W-5 — Copy of Office Order dated 7.0.203 


7. On the other hand the management has examined MW-! Ghanshyam Prasad Sinha in 
support of his case and submitted following documentary evidence: 


Exhibit -। — Copy of Office Order dated 28..999 


Exhibit M-2 — Copy of Letter dated 4.09.200I written by Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda 
Area to the ALC (C) Dhanbad in case of non-regularization of the workman Sushil Kumar Singh. 


8. Heard both sides and perused the materials on record. 


9. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the workman has submitted that the workman Sushil Kumar 
Singh has been shown as Sampling Attendant in the Office Order dated 28.!.999 but that is an 
error which was corrected later on vide office order dated 3.07.2006 and his designation is 
Sampling Assistant not Sampling Attendant. The management is taking from him the job of 
supervision of wagon under loading and over loading since 999 but he has still not been regularized 
as loading supervisor/loading munshi like that of Sri Y.P. Singh and Kapildeo Singh. His work is of 
permanent nature and therefore claimed his regularization. 


0. On the other hand the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the management has submitted that the 
workman Sushil Kumar Singh is Sampling Attendant and so he cannot be regularized at the post of 
loading supervisor/loading munshi because nature of job of both these post are different from each 
other and prayed to reject the claim of the workman. 


Il. On perusal of the documentary evidence of the workman i.e. Exhibit १४-। which is office 
order dated 07.07.2006 issued by the Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda Area it transpires that 
the workman Sushil Kumar Singh who was previously transferred from Dhansar Colliery to Area 
Office vide letter dated 03.06.2006 is hereby re-posted at Gondudih Colliery in his existing capacity 
under Sales & Dispatch Department keeping in view the Ref. Case No. 53 of 2002 and accordingly 


[भाग I—a€ve 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 5, 2026/ श्रावण 24, 948 94i] 


he was released from Area Office w.e.f. !0.07.2006 with directive to report for duty to Project 
Officer/Agent, Gondudih Colliery. Exhibit W-2 is the Office Order dated 3.07.2006 issued by Dy. 
Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda Area and on its perusal it is evident that the designation of the 
workman Sushil Kumar Singh that has been indicated as Sampling Mazdoor in the Office Order 
dated 07.07.2006 should be read as Sampling Assistant and thus it is clear that his correct 
designation is Sampling Assistant and not Sampling Attendant or Mazdoor that has been mentioned 
in the written statement of both the parties as well as in the Office Order dated 07.07.2006. Exhibit 
W-3 is the Office Order dated 8.07.2006 issued by the Project Officer, Gondudih Colliery which 
shows that Sushil Kumar Singh has now been transferred to Gondudih Colliery in his existing 
capacity under Sales & Dispatch Department and therefore he is directed to report for his duty to the 
Manager Gondudih Colliery for further assignment of work. Exhibit W-4 is the Office Order dated 
7.08.2006 and by this order the workman Sushil Kumar Singh, Sampling Assistant and one Sri 
Satrudhan Singh, Loading Clerk in Gondudih Colliery have been directed to supervise the coal 
transporting work from the Gondudih Colliery coal stock to the Railway Siding, K.D.S.-2 and 
maintain the entire record of the same and keep the same. Exhibit W-5 is the Office Order dated 
7.0.203 issued by the Project Officer, Gondudih Colliery by which the workman Sushil Kumar 
Singh was attached with Md. Sagir Alam, Sr. Manager (Mining), Gondudih Khas Kusunda Colliery 
and he will work under his supervision. 


2. As regards the evidence of the management, MW-Il Ghanshyam Prasad Sinha who is 
working as Welfare Inspector at Kusunda Area Office of M/s. BCCL has deposed that the workman 
was initially appointed in the office of coal controller and on its closure the workman was transferred 
to Dhansar Colliery siding in the year !999 vide office order dated 28..999 and his duty was to 
collect sample from the siding and get it tested from the laboratory. Though he was asked to look 
after the loading and unloading of wagons at Dhansar Siding as per office order but he could not 
perform the same and preferred the job of sampling attendant and accordingly he did the same. The 
salary of the workman is that of the sampling attendant which he was getting while working at the 
office of the coal controller. The work of sampling attendant is not that of loading munshi/loading 
supervisor and he is not legally entitled for regularization as such as he was transferred from coal 
controller office after its closure. In cross-examination he has stated that he cannot say all details of 
the area that the concerned workman is working in Dhansar Colliery. He has denied the suggestion 
that the workman is looking after the job of loading supervisor. 


3. The documentary evidence of the management i.e. Exhibit -। which is the Office Order 
dated 28..999 issued by the Project Officer Dhansar/Industry Colliery says that vide office order 
no. 2849 dated 22..999 of the Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda Area, the workman 
namely Sushil Kumar Singh and 3 others named therein who have been posted in Dhansar shall be 
doing the work that has been mentioned against their name and designation at Dhansar Siding and 
they will contact the concerned officer of Dhansar Siding for their work. Exhibit M-2 is the letter 
dated 4.09.200l written by the Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda Area to the ALC (C) 
Dhanbad regarding the industrial dispute for non-regularization of Sri Sushil Kumar Singh and in 
Paragraph-2 of the same he has admitted that Sushil Kumar Singh has been directed to look after the 
job of wagon loading at Dhansar Siding inter-alia. 


4. Admittedly the concerned workman was appointed initially in the office of coal controller 
and on its closure he was transferred to Dhansar Colliery siding in the year 999 vide office order 
no. 799 dated 28..999 (Exhibit M-) and at the same time on perusal of Exhibit W-2 which is 
office order dated 3.07.2006 issued by Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda Area it is clear that 
his designation was Sampling Assistant though by mistake on several places it has been wrongly 
mentioned as Sampling Attendant and the Office Order dated 28..999 (फटा. ]) is self-evident 
that the workman Sushil Kumar Singh was placed to supervise the work of wagon under loading/ 
over loading and that is why the reference order speaks about the adjudication whether the workman 
is entitled for regularization on the post of Loading Supervisor/Loading Munshi. Office Order dated 
7.08.2006 (Exhibit W-4) also makes it clear that after the workman Sushil Kumar Singh was 
transferred to Gondudih Colliery he was again deputed to supervise the work of coal transporting 
and maintain the entire record for the same. In Paragraph-2 of the letter dated 4.09.200] issued by 
Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kusunda Area in the name of ALC (C) Dhanbad (Exhibit M-2) also 
the management has admitted that the workman Sushil Kumar Singh has been directed to look after 
the job of Wagon Loading at Dhansar Siding and ७०७४ has also admitted the same though he 
further added that but the workman preferred the job of sampling attendant but he has no 
corroborating documentary evidence of it that he preferred to act as sampling attendant instead of the 
assigned job of supervision of loading and unloading of wagon so this portion of his oral evidence 
can not be relied and so all these things go to establish that though the designation of the workman 
Sushil Kumar Singh was Sampling Assistant, since the year 999 itself he was doing the work of 


942 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : AUGUST 5, 2026/ SHRAVAN 24, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


supervision of the wagon loading /unloading and as the work of supervision of wagon loading and 
unloading is perennial and permanent nature of job and the concerned workman is doing this job for 
such a long time, this Tribunal is of the opinion that he is entitled for regularization as Loading 
Munshi. 


5. Thus on the basis of the above discussion of the facts, circumstances and materials available on 
the case record this Tribunal finds and holds that the action of the management of M/s. BCCL in not 
regularizing Sri Sushil Kumar Singh as Loading Supervisor/Loading Munshi is neither fair nor 
justified and he is entitled to be regularized as Loading Munshi since January 200. The reference is 
answered accordingly.
